question.text: In the depository settlement process, 'pay-out' refers to:

answer.text: The CC transferring securities to the buying broker's CM account for securities bought on behalf of clients
The broker paying commission to the exchange
The investor paying margin to the CC
The DP paying fees to SEBI

explanation.text: The Logic: In the depository settlement process, pay-out is the transfer of securities by the Clearing Corporation to the buying broker's CM (Clearing Member) account for securities bought on behalf of clients. The buying broker then transfers these securities to the buyers. The Trap: Funds movement to selling brokers takes place outside the depository system, so wording that mixes funds and securities pay-out in the depository context is incorrect. Note: Pay-in and pay-out happen at designated times after the CC has netted all obligations.
